precepts.text: Paul went days without eating, and when he had received meat, he was strengthened; food and drink after the trial revive the servant of the Most High.
precepts.point: He called the name of that place En-hakkore, which is in Lehi unto this day.

note.label: Judges 15: The Jawbone of an Ass

precepts.why: When Samson had drunk, “his spirit came again, and he revived”. You kill a thousand men with a jawbone, you are going to be parched. It is the same as after a fast, when the first food and drink make you feel like a whole new person. Paul went days without eating, “And when he had received meat, he was strengthened.” Food and drink after the trial revive the servant of the Most High. Samson called on the Lord in his thirst, God clave an hollow place in the jaw and gave him water, and he called the name of that place En-hakkore, which is in Lehi unto this day.

precepts.text: Saul desired letters to Damascus so that if he found any of this way, whether men or women, he might bring them bound to Jerusalem; the sisters were persecuted too, not only the men.
precepts.point: Therefore they that were scattered abroad went every where preaching the word. Because of the great persecution the disciples had to flee, and our fathers were fugitives, always on the run, the way it was done to men like Nat Turner. It is going to come to that point again, where a brother might have to house a teacher whose name is on the news, wanted for sedition; you might be charged as guilty by association, but you have to see past it to protect your brother, because the gospel has to go forward. This is why we need such a high level of unity and love for one another to survive.

note.label: Acts 8: The Word Scattered Abroad, and the Baptism unto the Conscience

precepts.why:
Saul “desired of him letters to Damascus to the synagogues, that if he found any of this way, whether they were men or women, he might bring them bound unto Jerusalem.” The sisters were persecuted too, not only the men. Any of this way, men or women, were to be brought bound to Jerusalem.

This is the persecution that scattered them abroad, and it is coming again. That is why we need such a high level of unity and love for one another, brothers and sisters, to survive it and keep the gospel going forward.

precepts.text: Christ is the way, the truth, and the life, so those who followed him were called "this way."
precepts.point: Before the followers of Christ were called Christians in Acts 11, they were called "this way," meaning the way of Christ. Some people, when the persecution comes, will change their name back, stop wearing fringes, stop keeping the Sabbath, and hide, saying "that's not me."
precepts.why:
Before the followers of Christ were called Christians in Acts 11, they were called “this way”, meaning the way of Christ, because Christ said, “I am the way, the truth, and the life: no man cometh unto the Father, but by me.” That is who Saul was hunting with letters to Damascus: any of this way, whether men or women, to be brought bound unto Jerusalem.

This is why we tell brothers and sisters both to gird up their minds and build their faith by studying. When they notice you by your last name or your fringes, you will be persecuted. Some people, when the persecution comes, will change their name back, stop wearing fringes, stop keeping the Sabbath and hide, saying that's not me.

precepts.text: Paul's own retelling: those with him saw the light and were afraid but heard not the voice, the other half of the same account.
precepts.point: It was a caravan of men. Based on each man's account, one group heard the voice but saw no man, and another group saw the light but heard no voice, just as men running from the same scene report different pieces of it. There is no contradiction in the Bible.
precepts.why:
People read Acts 9:7 against Paul's own retelling in Acts 22 and claim a contradiction. Here the men “stood speechless, hearing a voice, but seeing no man.” There Paul says, “they that were with me saw indeed the light, and were afraid; but they heard not the voice of him that spake to me.” There is no contradiction.

It was a caravan of men. Based on each man's account, one group heard the voice but saw no man, and another group saw the light but heard no voice, just as men running from the same scene report different pieces of it. Acts 22 is the other half of the same account: “suddenly there shone from heaven a great light round about me”, Saul fell to the ground and heard the voice say, “Saul, Saul, why persecutest thou me?”, and the answer, “I am Jesus of Nazareth, whom thou persecutest.” There is no contradiction in the Bible.

precepts.text: When the voice came from heaven, some said it thundered and others said an angel spake, two witness accounts of one event.
precepts.point: It was a caravan of men. Based on each man's account, one group heard the voice but saw no man, and another group saw the light but heard no voice, just as men running from the same scene report different pieces of it. There is no contradiction in the Bible.
precepts.why:
The same thing happened when Christ prayed, “Father, glorify thy name. Then came there a voice from heaven, saying, I have both glorified it, and will glorify it again.” One event, and two witness accounts: “The people therefore, that stood by, and heard it, said that it thundered: others said, An angel spake to him.”

Some heard thunder, others heard an angel, from the same voice. So with Saul's caravan: some heard a voice but saw no man, and some saw the light but heard no voice. Different men report different pieces of the same scene; that is not a contradiction.

precepts.text: Christ was seen of Cephas, the twelve, above five hundred brethren, James, and all the apostles, and last of all he was seen of Paul, years after the resurrection.
precepts.point: Saul arose from the earth, and when his eyes were opened he saw no man, so they led him by the hand into Damascus. He was struck blind by what he witnessed.
precepts.why:
Saul was struck blind by what he witnessed. Paul counts what he saw among the appearances of the risen Christ: “he was seen of Cephas, then of the twelve: After that, he was seen of above five hundred brethren at once”, then “he was seen of James; then of all the apostles. And last of all he was seen of me also, as of one born out of due time.”

Christ was seen of Cephas, the twelve, above five hundred brethren, James and all the apostles, and last of all he was seen of Paul, years after the resurrection. That is what happened on the road: Saul saw the risen Christ, and when his eyes were opened he saw no man, so they led him by the hand into Damascus.

precepts.text: Judge nothing before the time, until the Most High brings to light the hidden things and makes manifest the counsels of the hearts.
precepts.point: This is the true meaning of loving your enemies. Christianity twists it to mean love the ones who enslaved, raped, and colonized your ancestors, stole your nationality, land, and heritage, miseducated you, gave you a false image of God, and today shut down anyone who says Israel is the true children of God. That is not the enemy the scripture means. The Bible means love the enemies within your own nation, because Paul, who persecuted and killed the disciples, was one of those enemies who could still repent.
precepts.why:
Ananias had heard by many how much evil Saul had done to the saints at Jerusalem. Saul had consented to Stephen's death and chased the disciples from city to city with zeal. Was he doing it in ignorance? Yes. That is why the scripture says, “judge nothing before the time, until the Lord come, who both will bring to light the hidden things of darkness, and will make manifest the counsels of the hearts”.

The things we all did in the world were worthy of death, so who are we to say a man is beyond repentance? The killer, even a pastor putting us to death in the future, may come to the truth later and say he did it in ignorance, as Christ and Stephen both prayed, Father, forgive them. Even a sister who cursed the teacher out on the streets for months came around and began to listen, because anyone can repent. Leave the judging to the Most High, who will make manifest the counsels of the hearts.

precepts.text: Love your enemies, bless them that curse you, pray for them that persecute you, that you may be the children of your Father, who gives time and chance to both the just and the unjust.
precepts.point: This is the true meaning of loving your enemies. Christianity twists it to mean love the ones who enslaved, raped, and colonized your ancestors, stole your nationality, land, and heritage, miseducated you, gave you a false image of God, and today shut down anyone who says Israel is the true children of God. That is not the enemy the scripture means. The Bible means love the enemies within your own nation, because Paul, who persecuted and killed the disciples, was one of those enemies who could still repent.
precepts.why:
“Ye have heard that it hath been said, Thou shalt love thy neighbour, and hate thine enemy. But I say unto you, Love your enemies, bless them that curse you, do good to them that hate you, and pray for them which despitefully use you, and persecute you; That ye may be the children of your Father which is in heaven: for he maketh his sun to rise on the evil and on the good, and sendeth rain on the just and on the unjust.” The Father gives time and chance to both the just and the unjust, and Saul, persecuting the saints with authority from the chief priests, was given his.

This is the true meaning of loving your enemies. Christianity twists it to mean love the ones who enslaved, raped and colonized your ancestors, stole your nationality, land and heritage, miseducated you, gave you a false image of God, and today shut down anyone who says Israel is the true children of God. That is not the enemy the scripture means. The Bible means love the enemies within your own nation, because Paul, who persecuted and killed the disciples, was one of those enemies who could still repent.

precepts.text: As concerning the gospel they are enemies for your sakes, but as touching the election they are beloved for the fathers' sakes, because they can still repent.
precepts.point: This is the true meaning of loving your enemies. Christianity twists it to mean love the ones who enslaved, raped, and colonized your ancestors, stole your nationality, land, and heritage, miseducated you, gave you a false image of God, and today shut down anyone who says Israel is the true children of God. That is not the enemy the scripture means. The Bible means love the enemies within your own nation, because Paul, who persecuted and killed the disciples, was one of those enemies who could still repent.
precepts.why:
“As concerning the gospel, they are enemies for your sakes: but as touching the election, they are beloved for the fathers’ sakes.” Enemies as concerning the gospel, yet beloved as touching the election, because they can still repent. That is the enemy Christ meant when he said love your enemies: the enemy within your own nation.

Saul was exactly that. He held authority from the chief priests to bind all that called on the name, an enemy of the gospel, and yet beloved for the fathers' sakes, and he repented. Not the ones who enslaved and colonized your ancestors, but your own people who fight the truth, may still come to it.

precepts.text: Paul's own confession: he shut up the saints in prison, gave his voice against them when put to death, punished them in every synagogue, and compelled them to blaspheme.
precepts.point: This is the true meaning of loving your enemies. Christianity twists it to mean love the ones who enslaved, raped, and colonized your ancestors, stole your nationality, land, and heritage, miseducated you, gave you a false image of God, and today shut down anyone who says Israel is the true children of God. That is not the enemy the scripture means. The Bible means love the enemies within your own nation, because Paul, who persecuted and killed the disciples, was one of those enemies who could still repent.
precepts.why:
Paul's own confession of what Ananias had heard by many: “many of the saints did I shut up in prison, having received authority from the chief priests; and when they were put to death, I gave my voice against them. And I punished them oft in every synagogue, and compelled them to blaspheme; and being exceedingly mad against them, I persecuted them even unto strange cities.”

He shut up the saints in prison, gave his voice against them when they were put to death, punished them in every synagogue and compelled them to blaspheme, chasing them from city to city with zeal. Ananias was right about the man, and still that man repented. The things we all did in the world were worthy of death, so who are we to say a man is beyond repentance?

precepts.text: Wisdom and knowledge shall be the stability of thy times, keeping us stabilized and focused for what is coming.
precepts.point: This is the true meaning of loving your enemies. Christianity twists it to mean love the ones who enslaved, raped, and colonized your ancestors, stole your nationality, land, and heritage, miseducated you, gave you a false image of God, and today shut down anyone who says Israel is the true children of God. That is not the enemy the scripture means. The Bible means love the enemies within your own nation, because Paul, who persecuted and killed the disciples, was one of those enemies who could still repent.
precepts.why:
“And wisdom and knowledge shall be the stability of thy times, and strength of salvation: the fear of the Lord is his treasure.” Wisdom and knowledge are what keep us stabilized and focused for what is coming.

A man like Saul, with authority from the chief priests to bind all that call on the name, will rise again, even a pastor putting us to death. Wisdom and knowledge keep us steady through it: judge nothing before the time, love the enemies within your own nation, and know that anyone can repent.

precepts.text: Paul, an apostle not of men, neither by man, but by Jesus Christ and God the Father who raised him from the dead.
precepts.point: Ananias enters, lays his hands on him as "Brother Saul," and immediately something like scales fall from his eyes, he receives sight, and is baptized. Paul was not taught by Peter or the other apostles; Christ himself taught him directly.
precepts.why: “Paul, an apostle, (not of men, neither by man, but by Jesus Christ, and God the Father, who raised him from the dead;)”. Paul was not taught by Peter or the other apostles. Christ himself taught him directly, and Ananias says the same when he comes in: it was “the Lord, even Jesus, that appeared unto thee in the way as thou camest” who sent him, that Saul might receive his sight and be filled with the Holy Ghost.

precepts.text: The gospel Paul preached was not after man; he received it by the revelation of Jesus Christ, not from any man.
precepts.point: Ananias enters, lays his hands on him as "Brother Saul," and immediately something like scales fall from his eyes, he receives sight, and is baptized. Paul was not taught by Peter or the other apostles; Christ himself taught him directly.
precepts.why:
“But I certify you, brethren, that the gospel which was preached of me is not after man. For I neither received it of man, neither was I taught it, but by the revelation of Jesus Christ.” The gospel Paul preached he received by the revelation of Jesus Christ, not from any man.

That is what began here, when the scales fell from his eyes and he received sight. Ananias laid hands on him and he was baptized, but Paul was not taught by Peter or the other apostles; Christ taught him directly.

precepts.text: Paul's own resume: beyond measure he persecuted and wasted the church of God, profiting in the Jews' religion above his equals, zealous of the traditions of his fathers.
precepts.point: Ananias enters, lays his hands on him as "Brother Saul," and immediately something like scales fall from his eyes, he receives sight, and is baptized. Paul was not taught by Peter or the other apostles; Christ himself taught him directly.
precepts.why:
Paul's own resume of who he was before this: “ye have heard of my conversation in time past in the Jews’ religion, how that beyond measure I persecuted the church of God, and wasted it: And profited in the Jews’ religion above many my equals in mine own nation, being more exceedingly zealous of the traditions of my fathers.”

Beyond measure he persecuted and wasted the church of God, profiting in the Jews' religion above his equals and zealous of the traditions of his fathers. This is the man Ananias lays hands on and calls Brother Saul, and the man Christ himself would teach.

precepts.text: Our religion was always the law and the ordinances of the fathers, never the man-made traditions taught in slavery.
precepts.point: Ananias enters, lays his hands on him as "Brother Saul," and immediately something like scales fall from his eyes, he receives sight, and is baptized. Paul was not taught by Peter or the other apostles; Christ himself taught him directly.
precepts.why:
What was the Jews' religion Paul profited in? “God forbid that we should forsake the law and the ordinances. We will not hearken to the king’s words, to go from our religion, either on the right hand, or the left.” Our religion was always the law and the ordinances of the fathers, never the man-made traditions taught in slavery.

So when Paul speaks of profiting in the Jews' religion, that is the law and the ordinances. Saul kept it zealously before Christ appeared to him in the way, and Christ, not the apostles, taught him from there.

precepts.text: Paul was brought up at the feet of Gamaliel, taught according to the perfect manner of the law of the fathers.
precepts.point: Ananias enters, lays his hands on him as "Brother Saul," and immediately something like scales fall from his eyes, he receives sight, and is baptized. Paul was not taught by Peter or the other apostles; Christ himself taught him directly.
precepts.why:
Paul was “brought up in this city at the feet of Gamaliel, and taught according to the perfect manner of the law of the fathers, and was zealous toward God”. Under Gamaliel he was taught the law of the fathers in its perfect manner.

But the gospel he was not taught by Peter or the other apostles. When Ananias laid hands on him and the scales fell from his eyes, it was Christ himself, who appeared to him in the way, who taught him directly.

precepts.text: Circumcised the eighth day, of the stock of Israel, the tribe of Benjamin, a Hebrew of the Hebrews, a Pharisee, and touching the righteousness in the law blameless.
precepts.point: Saul spends certain days with the disciples at Damascus and straightway preaches Christ in the synagogues, that he is the Son of God. Paul constantly has to give his resume, because he came up under Christ, not under the apostles, so the churches needed to know where he came from.
precepts.why:
Paul constantly has to give his resume, because he came up under Christ, not under the apostles, so the churches needed to know where he came from. “Circumcised the eighth day, of the stock of Israel, of the tribe of Benjamin, an Hebrew of the Hebrews; as touching the law, a Pharisee; Concerning zeal, persecuting the church; touching the righteousness which is in the law, blameless.”

Circumcised the eighth day, of the stock of Israel, the tribe of Benjamin, a Hebrew of the Hebrews, a Pharisee, and touching the righteousness in the law blameless. This is the man who, straightway after certain days with the disciples at Damascus, preached Christ in the synagogues, that he is the Son of God.

precepts.text: They shall offer sacrifices of righteousness, the righteousness that is within the law of sacrifice.
precepts.point: Saul spends certain days with the disciples at Damascus and straightway preaches Christ in the synagogues, that he is the Son of God. Paul constantly has to give his resume, because he came up under Christ, not under the apostles, so the churches needed to know where he came from.
precepts.why:
“They shall call the people unto the mountain; there they shall offer sacrifices of righteousness”. The righteousness Paul was blameless in is the righteousness that is within the law of sacrifice: the sacrifices of righteousness.

That is part of the resume Paul had to give. He kept the law of sacrifice blamelessly as a Pharisee, and the churches needed to know that about the man now preaching Christ in the synagogues.

precepts.text: Offer the sacrifices of righteousness, the law of sacrifice Paul kept blamelessly.
precepts.point: Saul spends certain days with the disciples at Damascus and straightway preaches Christ in the synagogues, that he is the Son of God. Paul constantly has to give his resume, because he came up under Christ, not under the apostles, so the churches needed to know where he came from.
precepts.why:
“Offer the sacrifices of righteousness, and put your trust in the Lord.” The sacrifices of righteousness are the law of sacrifice, and that is the law Paul kept blamelessly, touching the righteousness which is in the law.

Paul had to give this resume again and again because he came up under Christ and not under the apostles. A man blameless in the law of sacrifice was now preaching in the synagogues that Christ is the Son of God.

precepts.text: When it pleased the Most High, who separated Paul from his mother's womb and called him by grace, to reveal his Son in him that he might preach among the heathen.
precepts.point: All who heard were amazed, asking if this is not the same man who destroyed those who called on Christ's name. But Saul increased the more in strength and confounded the Jews at Damascus, proving that this is very Christ. He already knew the scriptures under Gamaliel; when Christ was revealed, everything started to make sense and he took it to another level.
precepts.why:
“But when it pleased God, who separated me from my mother’s womb, and called me by his grace, To reveal his Son in me, that I might preach him among the heathen; immediately I conferred not with flesh and blood”. The Most High separated Paul from his mother's womb and called him by grace, to reveal his Son in him that he might preach among the heathen.

That is why Saul increased the more in strength and confounded the Jews at Damascus, proving that this is very Christ. He already knew the scriptures under Gamaliel; when Christ was revealed in him, everything started to make sense and he took it to another level.

precepts.text: Before I formed thee in the belly I knew thee, and ordained thee a prophet unto the nations; the spirit was known before conception.
precepts.point: All who heard were amazed, asking if this is not the same man who destroyed those who called on Christ's name. But Saul increased the more in strength and confounded the Jews at Damascus, proving that this is very Christ. He already knew the scriptures under Gamaliel; when Christ was revealed, everything started to make sense and he took it to another level.
precepts.why:
“Before I formed thee in the belly I knew thee; and before thou camest forth out of the womb I sanctified thee, and I ordained thee a prophet unto the nations.” The spirit was known before conception. Jeremiah was sanctified and ordained a prophet before he came out of the womb, and Paul says the same of himself, separated from his mother's womb.

So the man who confounded the Jews at Damascus, proving that this is very Christ, was set apart for it before he was formed. What he learned under Gamaliel came alive when Christ was revealed.

precepts.text: The fear of the Most High to keep his commandments was created in the elect from the womb.
precepts.point: All who heard were amazed, asking if this is not the same man who destroyed those who called on Christ's name. But Saul increased the more in strength and confounded the Jews at Damascus, proving that this is very Christ. He already knew the scriptures under Gamaliel; when Christ was revealed, everything started to make sense and he took it to another level.
precepts.why:
“To fear the Lord is the beginning of wisdom: and it was created with the faithful in the womb.” The fear of the Most High to keep his commandments was created in the elect from the womb.

That is what was in Saul, separated from his mother's womb. He had the scriptures under Gamaliel, and when Christ was revealed, that fear created in him from the womb took it to another level, so he increased the more in strength and confounded the Jews.

precepts.text: Flesh and blood did not reveal Christ to Peter, but the Father, because only the Most High could give understanding already placed in him to receive.
precepts.point: All who heard were amazed, asking if this is not the same man who destroyed those who called on Christ's name. But Saul increased the more in strength and confounded the Jews at Damascus, proving that this is very Christ. He already knew the scriptures under Gamaliel; when Christ was revealed, everything started to make sense and he took it to another level.
precepts.why:
“Blessed art thou, Simon Bar–jona: for flesh and blood hath not revealed it unto thee, but my Father which is in heaven.” Flesh and blood did not reveal Christ to Peter; the Father did, because only the Most High could give understanding already placed in him to receive.

It was the same with Saul. He already knew the scriptures under Gamaliel, but it took the Father revealing his Son in him for everything to make sense, and then he confounded the Jews at Damascus, proving that this is very Christ.

precepts.text: The Spirit of Christ was always in them, testifying beforehand of his sufferings and the glory to follow.
precepts.point: All who heard were amazed, asking if this is not the same man who destroyed those who called on Christ's name. But Saul increased the more in strength and confounded the Jews at Damascus, proving that this is very Christ. He already knew the scriptures under Gamaliel; when Christ was revealed, everything started to make sense and he took it to another level.
precepts.why:
The prophets were “Searching what, or what manner of time the Spirit of Christ which was in them did signify, when it testified beforehand the sufferings of Christ, and the glory that should follow.” The Spirit of Christ was always in them, testifying beforehand of his sufferings and the glory to follow.

That same Spirit was in Saul, separated from his mother's womb, and it is why the scriptures he knew under Gamaliel started to make sense once Christ was revealed. He increased the more in strength, proving from those scriptures that this is very Christ.

precepts.text: Both the righteous and the wicked suffer strait things, but only the righteous receive the reward.
precepts.point: Properly prepare your mind, because anything can happen at any moment and you must be ready to drop everything and leave. In the world men drove drunk and gang-banged unafraid of death, so do not now be a coward for the truth; the Most High controls death, and it is better to die for this truth than to die for nothing.
precepts.why:
“Nevertheless the righteous shall suffer strait things, and hope for wide: for they that have done wickedly have suffered the strait things, and yet shall not see the wide.” Both the righteous and the wicked suffer strait things, but only the righteous receive the reward.

Saul suffered them here. The Jews watched the gates day and night to kill him, and the disciples let him down by the wall in a basket by night. This is what you are in: your front door may be occupied and you may have to go down the window on a rope. Properly prepare your mind, because anything can happen at any moment and you must be ready to drop everything and leave.

In the world men drove drunk and gang-banged unafraid of death, so do not now be a coward for the truth. The Most High controls death, and it is better to die for this truth than to die for nothing; the wicked suffer the strait things too, and they shall not see the wide.

precepts.text: Paul did not go up to the apostles first, but went into Arabia and returned again to Damascus, teaching there before Jerusalem.
precepts.point: He goes to Peter and James specifically, the two closest men to Christ, the top apostle and the Lord's brother, so his witness would be established with the leadership.
precepts.why:
Acts does not tell us that Saul went to Arabia first; Paul fills in that detail himself. “Neither went I up to Jerusalem to them which were apostles before me; but I went into Arabia, and returned again unto Damascus.” He did not go up to the apostles first. He went into Arabia and returned again to Damascus, teaching there before Jerusalem.

So by the time Saul came to Jerusalem and assayed to join himself to the disciples, he had already been preaching boldly at Damascus, which is what Barnabas declared to the apostles.

precepts.text: After three years he went up to Jerusalem to see Peter and stayed with him fifteen days.
precepts.point: He goes to Peter and James specifically, the two closest men to Christ, the top apostle and the Lord's brother, so his witness would be established with the leadership.
precepts.why:
“Then after three years I went up to Jerusalem to see Peter, and abode with him fifteen days.” This is the visit to Jerusalem in Acts 9, and Paul tells us it was after three years, and that he went to see Peter specifically and stayed with him fifteen days.

He went to Peter, the top apostle, the one closest to Christ, so that his witness would be established with the leadership.

precepts.text: He saw none of the other apostles except James, the Lord's brother.
precepts.point: He goes to Peter and James specifically, the two closest men to Christ, the top apostle and the Lord's brother, so his witness would be established with the leadership.
precepts.why:
“But other of the apostles saw I none, save James the Lord’s brother.” Of the apostles Barnabas brought him to, Paul saw only Peter and James, the Lord's brother.

He went to those two specifically, the two closest men to Christ, the top apostle and the Lord's brother, so his witness of seeing the Lord in the way and preaching boldly at Damascus would be established with the leadership.

precepts.text: Paul swears before the Most High that he is not lying about what happened to him.
precepts.point: He goes to Peter and James specifically, the two closest men to Christ, the top apostle and the Lord's brother, so his witness would be established with the leadership.
precepts.why:
“Now the things which I write unto you, behold, before God, I lie not.” Paul swears before the Most High that he is not lying about what happened to him: Arabia, the return to Damascus, the three years, Peter and James.

The disciples at Jerusalem were afraid of him and believed not that he was a disciple, so Paul's account of how he came in had to be trustworthy, and he puts it under oath.

precepts.text: Afterward Paul came into the regions of Syria and Cilicia, still unknown by face to the churches of Judaea.
precepts.point: Saul speaks boldly in the name of the Lord Jesus and disputes against the Grecians, but they go about to slay him, so the brethren bring him down to Caesarea and send him to Tarsus. Caesarea sits on the coast of Israel bordering the region of Syria near Damascus.
precepts.why: “Afterwards I came into the regions of Syria and Cilicia; And was unknown by face unto the churches of Judea which were in Christ”. This is the brethren sending Saul from Caesarea to Tarsus. Caesarea sits on the coast of Israel bordering the region of Syria near Damascus, and Tarsus is in Cilicia, so Paul came into the regions of Syria and Cilicia, still unknown by face to the churches of Judaea.

precepts.text: Tarsus, Paul's birthplace, is a city in Cilicia, modern-day Mersin, Turkey.
precepts.point: Saul speaks boldly in the name of the Lord Jesus and disputes against the Grecians, but they go about to slay him, so the brethren bring him down to Caesarea and send him to Tarsus. Caesarea sits on the coast of Israel bordering the region of Syria near Damascus.
precepts.why: Paul is “a Jew, born in Tarsus, a city in Cilicia”. Tarsus, where the brethren sent him, was his birthplace, a city in Cilicia, modern-day Mersin, Turkey. When the Grecians went about to slay him, the brethren sent him home.

precepts.text: The head of Syria is Damascus, which places Caesarea Philippi and the Syrophenician region under that rule.
precepts.point: Saul speaks boldly in the name of the Lord Jesus and disputes against the Grecians, but they go about to slay him, so the brethren bring him down to Caesarea and send him to Tarsus. Caesarea sits on the coast of Israel bordering the region of Syria near Damascus.
precepts.why: “For the head of Syria is Damascus”. Damascus is the head of Syria, which places Caesarea Philippi and the Syrophenician region under that rule. Caesarea, where the brethren brought Saul down, sits on the coast of Israel bordering the region of Syria near Damascus, and from there he was sent forth to Tarsus.

precepts.text: The Most High exalts the horn of his people, the praise of all his saints, even the children of Israel; the saints are Israel.
precepts.point: Then the churches have rest throughout all Judaea, Galilee, and Samaria, are edified, and walking in the fear of the Lord and the comfort of the Holy Ghost, are multiplied.
precepts.why:
“He also exalteth the horn of his people, the praise of all his saints; even of the children of Israel, a people near unto him. Praise ye the Lord.” The saints are Israel, the children of Israel, a people near unto him.

So the churches throughout all Judaea, Galilee and Samaria that had rest, were edified and were multiplied, walking in the fear of the Lord and in the comfort of the Holy Ghost, are the saints of the Most High's people, Israel.

precepts.text: Saul sought letters to bind any of "this way," whether men or women, and bring them to Jerusalem.
precepts.point: Before the followers of Christ were called Christians in Antioch, they were called "this way."

note.label: Acts 11: The Gentiles Are Scattered Israel

precepts.why:
Before the followers of Christ were called Christians in Antioch, they were called “this way.”

Saul “desired of him letters to Damascus to the synagogues, that if he found any of this way, whether they were men or women, he might bring them bound unto Jerusalem.” He sought them in the synagogues, men and women, because they were Israelites who followed Christ. They were the way before they were Christians.

precepts.point: There are certain people chosen from the foundation of the world to preach this gospel.

note.label: Galatians 1: Paul's Apostleship and the True Gospel

precepts.why:
Paul calls himself “an apostle, (not of men, neither by man, but by Jesus Christ”. He was not taught Christ by the disciples and was not awakened by them; Christ himself awakened and taught him. Acts 9 shows the moment. Saul, “yet breathing out threatenings and slaughter against the disciples of the Lord”, got letters from the high priest to Damascus so that “if he found any of this way, whether they were men or women, he might bring them bound unto Jerusalem.”

On the road “suddenly there shined round about him a light from heaven: And he fell to the earth, and heard a voice saying unto him, Saul, Saul, why persecutest thou me?” He asked, “Who art thou, Lord?” and the answer was “I am Jesus whom thou persecutest: it is hard for thee to kick against the pricks.” Trembling and astonished, Saul asked, “Lord, what wilt thou have me to do?”

Christ himself stopped Paul in his tracks and revealed himself to him even after his death, because Paul played an extremely important role in the gospel. If you are of the elect, if you were commissioned to do a job from the beginning, no matter what point of life you are in, you are going to wake up and fulfill the scriptures.

precepts.point: There are certain people chosen from the foundation of the world to preach this gospel.

note.label: Galatians 1: Paul's Apostleship and the True Gospel

precepts.why:
When Ananias hesitated, the Lord said of Saul, “Go thy way: for he is a chosen vessel unto me, to bear my name before the Gentiles, and kings, and the children of Israel: For I will shew him how great things he must suffer for my name’s sake.”

That is Paul's apostleship “by Jesus Christ, and God the Father.” He was a chosen vessel, and his credentials were astounding, above any other person. The things revealed to him were not revealed to many; there were mysteries revealed to him on a level beyond the other disciples, and he was able to go to scriptures and history and show the correlation between the past and the present. There are certain people chosen from the foundation of the world to preach this gospel, and Paul was one of them.

precepts.point: After three years of teaching, Paul went up to Jerusalem to see Peter and stayed with him fifteen days. The apostles were not aware of what Paul had been doing; he was doing these things having not been taught by Peter and the others.

note.label: Galatians 1: Paul's Apostleship and the True Gospel

precepts.why:
Paul did not go up to Jerusalem to the apostles before him; he went into Arabia, because there were Israelites living in Arabia, and returned to Damascus. Acts 9 covers this period. After the spirit of Christ came upon him he started preaching immediately: “Then was Saul certain days with the disciples which were at Damascus. And straightway he preached Christ in the synagogues, that he is the Son of God.” Those who heard him were amazed, asking, “Is not this he that destroyed them which called on this name in Jerusalem”, But Saul “increased the more in strength, and confounded the Jews which dwelt at Damascus, proving that this is very Christ.”

He was confounding the elders, preaching boldly that Christ was the Lord, until “the Jews took counsel to kill him” and watched the gates day and night, and the disciples let him down by the wall in a basket.

Then, after three years of teaching, he went up to Jerusalem to see Peter. “And when Saul was come to Jerusalem, he assayed to join himself to the disciples: but they were all afraid of him, and believed not that he was a disciple.” Barnabas had to bring him to the apostles and declare “how he had seen the Lord in the way, and that he had spoken to him, and how he had preached boldly at Damascus in the name of Jesus.” The apostles were not aware of what Paul had been doing; he was doing these things having not been taught by Peter and the others.

moments.label: From Negroes to Gods from Earth to Gold

points: And disputed against the Grecians. Notice how he spoke like a lion. He spoke boldly. He didn't speak soft. Come on.
But they went about to slay him. And that's what's going to happen to us. When you speak boldly in the name of the Lord, guess what? Eventually they going to want to put hands on us. Come on.

note.label: From Negroes to Gods from Earth to Gold

points: Now, here's the part I wanted to get to. This is the result of good leadership. What's going to happen here? Watch this. Then had the churches rest throughout all Judea and Galilee and Samaria. And were edified. Uh-huh. And walking in the fear of the Lord. The church, everybody in the building, was walking in the fear of the Lord, and in the comfort of the Holy Ghost. They all had the spirit of the Lord on them, the Holy Ghost. And what happened? Were multiplied. And what? Were multiplied. And that's when brothers and sisters are going to come on in right there. That's right. And we all rolling in the same spirit. And those spirits on the outside that come in and they see, damn, I want to be a part of this right here. I want the same spirit these brothers and sisters got right here. I need that thing right here. That's some powerful stuff right there.

note.label: From Negroes to Gods from Earth to Gold

points: Saul is still breathing out threatenings and slaughter against the disciples, going to the high priest for letters to Damascus so he can bind any of "this way," whether men or women, and drag them bound to Jerusalem. This is why we tell brothers and sisters both to gird up their minds and build their faith by studying, because when they notice you by your last name or your fringes you will be persecuted.

As Saul journeys near Damascus a light from heaven, a chariot of the Most High, shines round about him, he falls to the earth, and hears a voice: "Saul, Saul, why persecutest thou me?" Christ was already dead at this time, yet he says "why persecutest thou me," because what you do to one of his little ones you do to him also.

Saul did not realize he was in error. He thought the disciples were bringing heresy, but it was not heresy, it was the New Covenant being introduced. Trembling and astonished, he immediately humbles himself and says, "Lord, what wilt thou have me to do."
The men journeying with Saul stood speechless, hearing a voice but seeing no man. People read this against Acts 22 and claim a contradiction, but there is none.

It was a caravan of men. Based on each man's account, one group heard the voice but saw no man, and another group saw the light but heard no voice, just as men running from the same scene report different pieces of it. There is no contradiction in the Bible.
Saul arose from the earth, and when his eyes were opened he saw no man, so they led him by the hand into Damascus. He was struck blind by what he witnessed.

Saul is three days without sight, neither eating nor drinking. The Most High speaks in a vision to a disciple at Damascus named Ananias and sends him to the street called Straight, to the house of Judas, to lay hands on Saul.

Saul himself is given a vision of Ananias coming to restore his sight. People are still given dreams and visions this way, some seeing a man show them truth before they understood it was about Israel.

Ananias objects: he has heard by many how much evil this man has done to the saints at Jerusalem, and that he holds authority from the chief priests to bind all who call on the Most High's name. Saul had consented to Stephen's death and chased disciples from city to city with zeal.

The Most High tells Ananias to go his way, for Saul is a chosen vessel to bear his name before the Gentiles, kings, and the children of Israel. People discredit Paul's writings, but the book of Acts credits and justifies them, so to throw out Paul you would have to throw out Acts too.
The Most High will show Saul how great things he must suffer for his name's sake. The teaching on the Gentiles is held for later, when Paul actually begins his ministry.

Ananias enters, lays his hands on him as "Brother Saul," and immediately something like scales fall from his eyes, he receives sight, and is baptized. Paul was not taught by Peter or the other apostles; Christ himself taught him directly.

Saul spends certain days with the disciples at Damascus and straightway preaches Christ in the synagogues, that he is the Son of God. Paul constantly has to give his resume, because he came up under Christ, not under the apostles, so the churches needed to know where he came from.

All who heard were amazed, asking if this is not the same man who destroyed those who called on Christ's name. But Saul increased the more in strength and confounded the Jews at Damascus, proving that this is very Christ. He already knew the scriptures under Gamaliel; when Christ was revealed, everything started to make sense and he took it to another level.

After many days the Jews take counsel to kill Saul, watching the gates day and night, so the disciples take him by night and let him down the wall in a basket. This is what you are in: your front door may be occupied and you may have to go down the window on a rope.

When Saul comes to Jerusalem he tries to join the disciples, but they are afraid of him until Barnabas brings him to the apostles and declares how he had seen the Lord and preached boldly at Damascus. Notice Acts does not tell us he went to Arabia first; Paul fills in that detail himself in Galatians.

Saul speaks boldly in the name of the Lord Jesus and disputes against the Grecians, but they go about to slay him, so the brethren bring him down to Caesarea and send him to Tarsus. Caesarea sits on the coast of Israel bordering the region of Syria near Damascus.
Then the churches have rest throughout all Judaea, Galilee, and Samaria, are edified, and walking in the fear of the Lord and the comfort of the Holy Ghost, are multiplied.

As Peter passes through all quarters he comes to the saints at Lydda and finds Aeneas, who had kept his bed eight years sick of the palsy. Peter says, "Aeneas, Jesus Christ maketh thee whole; arise and make thy bed," and he arises immediately.
All that dwelt at Lydda and Sharon saw him and turned to the Lord.

At Joppa a disciple named Tabitha, called Dorcas, full of good works and almsdeeds, falls sick and dies, and they wash her and lay her in an upper chamber. Women were disciples too, students and followers of Christ, and washing the dead shows our own customs of purifying the body.

Dorcas made coats and garments and gave almsdeeds, so she had a good name and no covetous spirit; what she took in she gave back. This is unlike the opportunists who see thousands at Passover and only think of what they can get from the people, coveting to live off of them.

The disciples send for Peter, who puts them all out, kneels, prays, and says, "Tabitha, arise." She opens her eyes and sits up, and he presents her alive to the saints and widows, so that many in Joppa believed. Peter then tarries many days in Joppa with Simon a tanner.
